questions.q: What event marked the official start of the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930?
questions.a: The Dandi March (or Salt March) marked the start of the movement. A wrong answer suggests the student has not yet associated the movement's beginning with Gandhi's specific journey to the coast.

questions.q: Why did Gandhi choose to break the salt law specifically, rather than any other law?
questions.a: He chose salt because it was a basic necessity used by everyone, rich or poor, and the British monopoly and tax on it represented how they exploited all Indians. A wrong answer shows the student does not understand that the protest was meant to connect with the daily lives of common people.

questions.q: If you were a villager in 1930, how would you show your support for this movement without using violence?
questions.a: Steps: 1. Acknowledge the need for non-violence. 2. Identify a peaceful action, like making salt at home or refusing to buy British-made goods. 3. Explain that this refusal is a form of 'disobedience.' A wrong answer indicates the student thinks 'disobedience' must involve fighting or physical harm.

questions.q: How does the term 'Civil Disobedience' differ from a violent rebellion?
questions.a: Civil Disobedience is the peaceful, public refusal to follow a law one believes is unjust, whereas violent rebellion involves force and destruction. A wrong answer reveals confusion between peaceful protest and armed conflict.

questions.q: Was the Dandi March an effective way to protest? Justify your answer.
questions.a: Yes, it was effective because it turned a simple, legal issue into a national movement that gathered widespread support through non-violence. A wrong answer suggests the student believes only physical force can make a political impact.

questions.q: Design a simple poster slogan that Gandhi might have used to explain the movement to villagers who could not read.
questions.a: The slogan should focus on 'Salt is our right' or 'Free salt for all.' A poor answer would be a complex essay or a violent slogan, which fails to capture the spirit of simple, non-violent mass participation.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The Civil Disobedience Movement was a non-violent protest started by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930 to challenge British rule by ______ breaking unfair laws, beginning with the salt tax.
Fill in the blank: ______ you are playing a game where someone suddenly makes a rule that you have to pay a fee every time you take a breath of air; would you follow that rule?

Fill in the blank: The Civil Disobedience Movement was a non-violent protest started by Mahatma Gandhi in ______ to challenge British rule by intentionally breaking unfair laws, beginning with the salt tax.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can identify the Dandi March as the starting point of the movement and explain why a common item like salt was chosen as a symbol of protest against British oppression.
